title: Running Sums
statement: You are given n integers. A running sum (also called a prefix sum) at position i is the sum of the first i numbers. Print all n running sums on one line, separated by single spaces. Try to use itertools.accumulate or a generator.
inputFormat: Line 1: an integer n. Line 2: n integers separated by spaces.
outputFormat: One line with n integers: the running sums, separated by single spaces.
constraints: Sums can be larger than 32 bits; Python integers handle this.
explanations: Start with 10. Then 10-3=7. Then 7+5=12. Then 12-12=0. The sum can go down when a number is negative.
reference:
import sys
from itertools import accumulate

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    print(" ".join(map(str, accumulate(nums))))

main()
